history.summary: Probably the oldest temple of the Muzaffarpur region, centred on a huge four-armed (Chaturbhuj) Vishnu idol said to be self-manifested (svayambhu). Regional lore says the idol was unearthed from a small pond near Turki village (~10 km from Muzaffarpur) and brought here by an unnamed local saint who was a devotee of Shiva, and placed beside a Shivling - the site grew into the present temple complex (which also houses Shiva, Surya, Bhairav and Bajrang Bali idols, per visitor reviews). Origin dates conflict (12th century vs 1303 CE) and no inscriptions verify the legend (flagged). Address: Goshala Road, Chandwara, Muzaffarpur-842001. Coordinates are approximate (Chaturbhuj Sthan Chowk anchor). No reliable on-topic photo found after genuine searching; media left empty.

name: Chaturbhuj Sthan Temple
town_description: Muzaffarpur is a major city in North Bihar and the commercial capital of the Tirhut region, famous worldwide for its Shahi litchi. It is a large railway junction about 70 km north of Patna.

travel.airport: Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport, Patna (about 70 km)
travel.road: At Chaturbhuj Sthan Chowk, Goshala Road, Chandwara, in the city centre; reachable by city road
